chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not a tyrant to His servants, and He is more Knowing of what is in the breasts, more Seeing of what is in the eyes, closer to what is in the bellies, and more Capable of what is in the earth and the heavens. Nothing is too difficult for Him, no force overcomes Him, and not the weight of an atom in the heavens or in the earth escapes Him, nor anything smaller or larger. Indeed, Allah is All-Seeing of what they do.

key_terms.الصُّدُور: The breasts/chests (metaphor for inner thoughts and intentions)
key_terms.ظَلَّامٍ: Tyrant or one who deals unjustly
key_terms.مِثْقَالُ ذَرَّةٍ: The weight of an atom (smallest measurable unit)

ai.seo_question: What are the key attributes of Allah regarding justice and knowledge mentioned in this narration?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this narration to anchor the Shia doctrine of divine justice (*Adl*) against the Mu'tazila and Ash'ari debates, affirming that Allah’s omnipotence is never arbitrary. By linking His absolute knowledge (*Ilm*) to His justice, the text clarifies that every action, from grand cosmic events to the subtlest inner thoughts, is known and accounted for without compulsion or tyranny.
